expected: First feasible-or-near-miss run: accuracy 0.750-0.758 and time 8-10 s (versus 0.012 and 0.10 s for the infeasible baseline). If accuracy is >=0.753 this becomes the incumbent. If it is a near-miss, the 9.5-epoch idea is the fix.
description: Replace the template with a full airbench port in submissions/arena/. Architecture: a frozen 2x2 patch-whitening first conv (eigenvectors computed in prepare from training images), Dirac-initialized convs, widths 128/384/576 with 3 convs per group, BN with a 64x bias LR, and a GAP+linear head scaled for 100 classes. Optimizer: Nesterov SGD at batch 1024 with lr 9.0 (airbench scaling), wd 0.012, Lookahead and a triangular LR. Training: label smoothing 0.3, alternating flip, random crop with 2 px translate, 8.5 epochs, no TTA. The full uint8 dataset lives on the GPU with augmentation done there. Use fp16 autocast and channels_last. torch.compile the train step in build and warm it up on synthetic data; use drop_last so batch shapes stay fixed. Eval uses an uncompiled (or dynamic=True) path so any B from 1 to 1024 avoids slow recompiles. Log prepare and train time separately.

expected: Accuracy rises by >=0.4 pp, to >=0.756, and time rises by <=12% (about +1 s). It should be safely feasible even if 8.5 epochs misses 0.753.
description: Same as the airbench port, with only the epoch count raised from 8.5 to 9.5. The triangular LR schedule stretches to match, and nothing else changes. This hedges the thin margin that the TTA ban leaves.

expected: 3-seed mean accuracy within ±0.2 pp of the first run, time within ±3%, per-seed std <=0.35 pp. The metrics should not improve; the value is information only.
description: Re-run the current incumbent airbench config unchanged, as a pure replicate, and record per-seed accuracies and per-trial prepare/train times. This calibrates the noise floor that every later delta is judged against.

expected: Accuracy within ±0.3 pp of the incumbent, and time within ±5% of it. If it is >5% faster and still >=0.753, H1.5 is refuted and the frontier moves toward wider and shorter.
description: On the feasible airbench incumbent, widen the last group from 576 to 768 channels (128/384/768) and cut epochs from the incumbent count to 7.5, with the LR schedule rescaled. Everything else is held fixed.

expected: Prepare time drops by >=0.1 s, to <=0.5 s in total, so total time falls by about 1-3%. Accuracy within ±0.2 pp.
description: On the incumbent, compute the patch-whitening covariance from a random 5000-image subset (drawn with the trial-seeded generator inside prepare) instead of all 50k. Also make the dataset transfer a single bulk uint8 copy to the GPU, with normalization fused into the train step. Report prepare time.

expected: Train time per epoch drops by 5-15% (total time about -0.5 to -1.2 s), and accuracy is unchanged within noise. If the recompiles log shows extra recompiles, removing them should save >=0.5 s.
description: Throughput ablation on the incumbent: switch the torch.compile mode from default to max-autotune, with autotuning done fully in the untimed build on synthetic batches of the exact training shapes (full batch plus any eval shapes used in train). Check with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles that zero recompiles happen in the timed region, which also covers H3.2.1.

expected: The prior favours SGD: accuracy >=0.3 pp below the incumbent at equal time. Upside case: Muon matches accuracy in >=10% less time, which would refute H1.4 and open a new optimizer branch.
description: Explore: on the incumbent architecture, replace Nesterov SGD on the conv weights with Muon (lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, 3 Newton-Schulz steps, batch 2000). Biases, BN and the head stay on SGD. Use the same epoch budget, tuned so wall time matches the SGD incumbent.

expected: Train time drops by about 15-20%, and accuracy drops by 0.2-0.6 pp. The run is useful only if the drop is <=0.3 pp. Otherwise, pair it with +0.5 epoch.
description: Explore: on the incumbent, train the first ~50% of epochs on 24 px random crops (downscaled from 32 px on the GPU), then 32 px for the rest. Compile and warm up both shapes in build.

expected: Accuracy 0.752-0.758, centred near 0.755. This comes from E004's 0.7389 at 7.5 epochs plus ~1 pp per epoch over 1.75 epochs, minus a little for diminishing returns. Time ~8.8-9.0 s: about 444 steps at ~20.1 ms/step with max-autotune, plus ~0.06 s prepare. If accuracy is >=0.753, this is the first feasible incumbent; next, step down 0.25 epochs at a time. If it lands at 0.750-0.753, go to 9.5 epochs.
description: Exploit, following E004's contingency. On the current incumbent (E006: subset whitening, max-autotune compile, fp16, channels_last), widen the last group from 576 to 768 channels (128/384/768). Set epochs to 9.25 and stretch the triangular LR to match. Everything else stays fixed: lr 9.0, wd 0.012, ls 0.3, Lookahead, alternating flip, batch 1024 with drop_last. Warm up the new shapes in build. Log ms/step.

expected: Per-step time ~21-22.5 ms (+5-10% over 768, not FLOP-proportional). With 408 steps that gives a time of ~8.7-9.2 s. Accuracy 0.750-0.758. If it matches the 768 / 9.25-epoch run's accuracy in >=3% less time, the optimum is wider still and 1280 should be tried. If accuracy falls below 768's on the epoch line, 768 is near the knee.
description: Exploit and probe the width frontier. Widen the last group further to 1024 (128/384/1024) and cut epochs to 8.5, with the LR schedule rescaled and everything else held at the incumbent. Group 3 runs at 8x8 and 4x4, where E004 showed widening is nearly free per step, so this tests whether extra width still buys sample efficiency.
note: Settled by E008: under the Muon incumbent, widening group 3 (576->768) at -0.5 epoch lost 0.3 pp and was 2% slower; a further widening to 1024 rests on the SGD-only width bonus (E004) that did not transfer.

expected: Per-step time falls 8-15%, saving ~0.7-1.2 s per trial. Accuracy falls 0.3-0.8 pp. The idea is a win if the loss is under ~1 pp per second saved, i.e. the result sits above the epoch line. If so, pair it with +0.5-0.75 epoch to recover feasibility at lower total time.
description: Exploit, cutting per-step cost where it is concentrated. E004's post-mortem found that the high-resolution group-1 layers (32x32 and 16x16) dominate step time. Cut group 1 from 3 convs to 2 (keep the pooling position and the 128 width). Run it on the best 768-wide config (I-768 at 9.25 epochs if that run is kept; otherwise on the incumbent), keeping the same epochs and everything else.

expected: Per-step time -6-12%. Accuracy -0.2 to -0.6 pp. This tells us whether group-1 width or group-1 depth is the cheaper thing to cut. If the accuracy loss per second saved is below ~1 pp/s, it beats adding epochs and should be combined with the winner of the group-1 depth cut.
description: Explore, as an alternative way to cheapen group 1. Keep 3 convs in group 1 but narrow its width from 128 to 96 channels (96/384/768, or 96/384/576 on the incumbent if the 768 run isn't kept). The whitening conv output and the group-2 input adjust to match. Same epochs, LR rescaled only as airbench's width-independent scaling dictates (unchanged).

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). H1.3.1 predicts accuracy drops by >=0.2 pp (to <=0.746 on the 576/9.5-epoch incumbent). If accuracy instead rises or stays within 0.1 pp, H1.3.1 is refuted, and ls 0.2 (or a 0.3->0.4 probe) becomes a free knob worth testing on the 768 net.
description: Explore. On the incumbent config, lower label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2 and change nothing else. This is a decisive test of H1.3.1, which has never been tested.

expected: Train time -10-13% (about -0.9 to -1.1 s). Accuracy falls by 0.1-0.6 pp. H1.6.1 holds if the fall is <=0.2 pp. Even a 0.3-0.5 pp fall is a net win at the ~1 pp/s exchange rate, if spending the saved time on epochs recovers more than that.
description: Explore. Add loss-based data filtering. During the second half of training, keep the per-example loss computed in the forward pass. Each epoch, drop the 25% lowest-loss examples from the previous epoch, so second-half epochs have fewer batches. Batches stay fixed at 1024 with drop_last, so no new shapes appear. The losses are a byproduct of training (no extra forward passes), and the selection runs on the GPU with the trial-seeded generator. Keep the LR schedule defined over the total number of steps.

expected: Per-step time is about 35 ms (E009), so time is about 8.4-8.5 s, versus 8.71 s for the incumbent. Accuracy should be 0.754-0.757: E009's 0.7515 plus 0.5 epoch at a Muon slope of about 0.6-1.0 pp/epoch. If accuracy is >=0.753, this is the new incumbent at about -3% time. If it is 0.750-0.753, go to 9.75 epochs.
description: Exploit; this combines the E009 near-miss with extra epochs. Start from the E007 Muon incumbent (128/384/576, Muon lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 / 3 NS steps, batch 2000, ls 0.3, alternating flip, max-autotune, subset whitening). Cut group 1 from 3 convs to 2, exactly as in E009 (same pooling position, width 128). Raise epochs from 9.0 to 9.5 (about 238 steps) and stretch the LR schedule to match. Change nothing else. Warm up the new shapes in build. Log ms/step and per-seed accuracy.

expected: From E011 (train 6.79 s at 9 epochs), a full-res epoch costs about 0.96 s and a 24 px epoch about 0.55 s. That puts time near 5.25x0.96 + 5.25x0.55 + 0.06 = about 8.0 s, roughly -8% against 8.71 s. Accuracy should be 0.753-0.758: 0.746 plus 1.5 epochs at about 0.5-0.8 pp/epoch. If it reaches >=0.753 it becomes the new incumbent. If it misses by <0.3 pp, try 11 epochs.
description: Exploit; this is E011's contingency. Progressive resizing on the Muon incumbent, with more total epochs. Use 10.5 epochs in total. Train the first 50% of epochs on whole augmented images downscaled to 24 px on the GPU (bilinear F.interpolate; AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) as in E011) and the rest at 32 px. Define the LR schedule over total steps. Compile with dynamic=False and warm up both shapes in build, so nothing recompiles in the timed region. Keep everything else at E007.

expected: Time about 8.25 s, -0.45 s. Accuracy 0.749-0.752, which implies a slope of 0.5-1.0 pp/epoch. If accuracy holds at >=0.753, the slope is under 0.3 pp/epoch, so epochs are a cheap knob under Muon and this becomes the incumbent. If so, try 8.0 epochs next.
description: Control to measure the exchange rate. Run the E007 Muon incumbent unchanged except for 8.5 epochs instead of 9.0 (about 213 steps), with the LR schedule stretched to match. This gives the Muon pp/epoch slope that E009, E010, E011 and E013 have to be re-scored against. It also tells us whether trimming epochs on 576 is itself a competitive way to cut time.
note: Settled by E009 -> E014: the Muon epoch slope was measured directly on the 2/3/3 net (+0.44 pp for +0.5 epoch, ~0.9 pp/epoch); E007 (3/3/3) is no longer the incumbent, so an 8.5-epoch control on it adds little.

expected: Accuracy rises by 0.1-0.4 pp, to about 0.755-0.758. Per-step time falls by about 1% because the Lookahead update goes away. If accuracy is >=+0.2 pp it becomes the new incumbent, and the extra margin can be spent on about 0.25-0.5 fewer epochs. If it falls by >0.2 pp, Lookahead or the warmup is doing work under Muon; next, split them apart.
description: On the E007 Muon incumbent at 9.0 epochs, remove Lookahead and replace the triangular warmup+decay schedule with linear decay from peak to 0, with no warmup, for both the Muon and SGD groups. That is airbench94_muon style. Keep lr, momentum, batch and epochs fixed. Make the change in one run, because both components are SGD-era carryovers.

expected: Accuracy +0.1 to +0.3 pp, about 0.755-0.757, from more optimizer steps at the same number of epochs. Time +1 to +3%, about 8.8-8.95 s, from more Newton-Schulz calls and smaller GEMMs. The idea wins only if the gain is >=0.2 pp. In that case trade the gain for -0.25 epoch.
description: Explore. On the E007 Muon incumbent, switch to batch 1536 with Muon lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655 (Hiverge settings). Use the same 9.0 epochs (drop_last, so about 292 steps) and scale the SGD-group lr linearly with batch size. Warm up the new batch shape in build.

expected: Train time -3 to -6%, about -0.25 to -0.5 s, removing most of the ~4% Muon overhead and Python launch cost. 3-seed mean accuracy stays within 0.1 pp of 0.7544. If the gain is <1%, launch overhead is not the bottleneck and H2.5 is weakened.
description: Throughput, numerically near-equivalent. Batch Newton-Schulz across conv weights by grouping same-shape weights into one batched matmul call. Use torch._foreach ops for the SGD updates on biases, BN and the head. Capture the full train step (forward, backward, Muon, SGD) in a CUDA graph with static input buffers, and warm it up in build on synthetic data. Pass the LR schedule as a GPU tensor so per-step LR changes need no recapture. prepare resets all parameter and state tensors in place.

expected: 3-seed mean +0.0 to +0.3 pp; per-seed std down >=30%, from about 0.25 to <=0.18 pp; time <=+2%. If the mean rises >=0.2 pp, keep it and spend the margin on fewer epochs. If the mean falls, EMA averages over too-high-LR iterates in this short schedule; drop H4.2.
description: Explore. On the E007 Muon incumbent, add a weight EMA that covers about the last epoch (decay about 0.99 per step at batch 2000, updated only in the final ~25% of steps). Also apply the EMA to the BN running statistics. Evaluate with the EMA weights. Run the EMA update as a single foreach op inside the compiled step. Reset the EMA in prepare.

expected: Trial 1's train time drops by about 0.1-0.15 s, to within 0.05 s of trials 2-3. Mean time falls about 0.05 s (about -0.6%), and accuracy is unchanged (bit-identical if the RNG streams are untouched). It is a small free gain, worth keeping if the drop is >=0.03 s.
description: In build, run 2-3 full optimizer steps on synthetic data: Muon/Newton-Schulz, momentum-buffer allocation, SGD groups, and the backward pass at the training batch shape. Then torch.cuda.synchronize. In prepare, re-init the parameters, buffers and optimizer state in place. Log per-trial train time.
note: Subsumed by E018 (I020): optimizer steps (SGD state, Muon graph) are now warmed in build; trial-1 train time (8.075 s) is no longer above trials 2-3 (8.096 / 8.124).

expected: Time about 7.5-7.7 s (-6 to -8%). That assumes about 0.85 s per full-res epoch and about 0.49 s per 24 px epoch: 5x0.49 + 6x0.85 + 0.06 prepare. Accuracy 0.754-0.758, centred near 0.756: E015's -0.43 pp from resizing, plus about +0.45 pp for the extra half full-res epoch, on top of 0.7571. If it reaches >=0.755, it becomes the incumbent; next, trim 0.5 full-res epochs. If it reaches 0.751-0.753, move to 5 low-res + 6.5 full-res epochs.
description: Exploit: add progressive resizing to the E018 incumbent (2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655, CUDA-graphed step, 9.5 epochs, 0.7571 @ 8.16 s). This is E015's contingency moved onto the faster, higher-margin base. Train 11 epochs in total. Epochs 1-5 use whole augmented images downscaled to 24 px on the GPU (bilinear F.interpolate, AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) head pooling as in E011/E015). Epochs 6-11 run at 32 px. Define the LR schedule (triangular plus Lookahead, as in the incumbent) over total steps. Batch 1536 with drop_last at both resolutions. Capture one CUDA graph per resolution in build and warm both on synthetic data, so nothing recompiles or recaptures in the timed region. Everything else stays at E018. Log per-phase ms/step.

expected: Time about 7.93-7.98 s (-2.5%, about -0.21 s). Accuracy 0.7535-0.7560, centred near 0.7549, from about 0.9 pp/epoch. If it holds >=0.7545, it becomes the incumbent and the slope is <=1 pp/epoch. If it falls below 0.753, the slope at this point is steeper (>1.6 pp/epoch), so stop trimming epochs and spend the margin only on per-step cuts.
description: Exploit the margin and measure the epoch slope on the current recipe. On E018, change only the epoch count, from 9.5 to 9.25 (32 steps/epoch at batch 1536 with drop_last, so 296 steps instead of 304), with the LR schedule stretched to match. Nothing else changes. The result gives the pp-per-second exchange rate on the graphed batch-1536 net, the reference for scoring every later per-step cut.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy +0.0 to +0.2 pp, about 0.757-0.759. If it gains >=0.15 pp, keep it and trade the gain for about -0.15 epoch. If it loses >=0.1 pp, the decay-to-zero tail is doing useful annealing in this short schedule; close H1.7.5.
description: On E018, set an LR floor: the decay phase ends at 5% of the peak LR instead of 0, for both the Muon group and the SGD groups (bias, BN, head). Shape: linear from the peak to 0.05x peak over the existing decay steps. Warmup, Lookahead, epochs and batch are unchanged. The LR tensor in the CUDA graph is just a different precomputed schedule, so nothing needs recapturing.
note: Premise wrong: the incumbent's airbench triangle already decays to 0.07x peak (not 0), so a 0.05x floor would only change the floor 0.07 -> 0.05, an effect far below the ~0.15-0.2 pp between-config trajectory noise (E020/E021).

expected: Accuracy +0.05 to +0.25 pp, about 0.7575-0.7595. Time +1 to +4% (about 8.25-8.45 s), since conv efficiency may start to drop at 1024. It wins only if the gain is >=0.2 pp per +1% time; then trade it for about -0.25 epoch. If accuracy is flat or lower, 1536 is the batch optimum; close the batch axis.
description: Explore whether smaller Muon batches keep buying accuracy now that per-step overhead is graphed away. E017 showed 2000 -> 1536 gave +0.16 pp at unchanged per-image cost. On E018, switch to batch 1024: Muon lr 0.205*sqrt(1024/1536) = 0.167 and momentum 0.70, with the SGD-group lr scaled linearly with batch. Keep 9.5 epochs (48 steps/epoch, 456 steps). Recapture the CUDA graph at the new batch shape in build.

expected: Per-step time -8 to -10% (one 16x16 conv, matching E009's 9%), so train time at 10.25 epochs is about 7.9-8.1 s (-1 to -3%). Accuracy 0.752-0.757: the cut probably costs more than E009's 0.29 pp because group 1 then has no 16x16 conv, recovered by about +0.7 pp from the extra epochs. It wins only if it is >=0.754 at <8.0 s. The profiler should show >=40% of GPU time in non-conv kernels at 32x32/16x16. If not, H2.4's memory-bandwidth mechanism is weakened.
description: Explore the next group-1 cut, extending E009's depth cut. On E018, reduce group 1 from 2 convs to 1, keeping only the 32x32 whitening-output -> 128 conv followed by pool/BN/GELU, and removing the remaining 16x16 128->128 conv. Raise epochs from 9.5 to 10.25 to compensate. Also record a one-step torch.profiler breakdown (conv vs BN/activation/pool kernels per stage) in the smoke test, which tests H2.4.1.

expected: Time unchanged (±1%). 3-seed mean within 0.7555-0.7590, and |delta| vs 0.7571 of 0.1-0.3 pp. A |delta| >=0.2 pp means every pending verdict with an effect <0.2 pp (E017, H1.7.5, epoch trims) must be treated as inconclusive, and a >=0.755 margin is required before keeping a time cut.
description: Noise calibration on the incumbent, with no recipe change. Add an internal salt to the data-order/augmentation generator (the trial seeds stay 0, 1, 2) and run E018 with salt=1. The pre-registered comparison is against E018's 0.7571 (salt 0); a second salt run is optional. Per-seed accuracies are logged.
note: ideate: Noise calibration against E018 (0.7571), which is no longer the tip. It is replaced by the same salt test on the E021 incumbent, where the margin (+0.22 pp) actually binds keep decisions.

expected: Muon time drops by about 0.3-0.45 ms/step over ~344 steps, so train time falls by about 0.1-0.15 s (-1.3 to -2%), to about 7.47-7.52 s. With preconditioning the accuracy change should be within ±0.15 pp of 0.7552, which is inside trajectory noise. Keep it if accuracy is >=0.7535 and time is >=1% lower. If accuracy drops by >0.25 pp, the 3rd NS step matters in this short schedule; close the NS-step axis.
description: Exploit, cheapening the per-step Muon cost (~2 ms/step of GPU time per the E018 profile, the same at 24 and 32 px). On the E021 incumbent (2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655, CUDA-graphed step, 5 epochs at 24 px + 5.75 at 32 px, 0.7552 @ 7.62 s), replace the 3-step Newton-Schulz with Turbo-Muon-style almost-orthogonal preconditioning followed by 2 NS steps (C0008/C0009). Before NS, rescale X's columns by 1/sqrt of the row sums of |X^T X|, inside the batched NS call. Keep the same NS coefficients for the 2 remaining steps, and keep lr, momentum and everything else fixed. Recapture both CUDA graphs in build. Log ms/step per phase.

expected: 28 px epochs cost about 0.66-0.70 s (77% of the pixels; 24 px cost 64% of a full epoch at 56% of the pixels). Time is about 2.7 + 1.37 + 3.38 + 0.06 = about 7.5 s (-1 to -2.5%). Accuracy is 0.753-0.757, centred near 0.755: about 9.45 full-epoch equivalents, the same as the incumbent. Keep it if it is >=0.7535 and faster. If it lands >=0.756, the next step is to move one more 32 px epoch to 28 px.
description: Exploit and test the untested intermediate-resolution step. On E021, change the resolution schedule from 5x24 px + 5.75x32 px to 5x24 px + 2x28 px + 4x32 px (11 epochs in total), with the LR schedule (triangle plus Lookahead) defined over total steps. Use whole augmented images downscaled with bilinear F.interpolate, as for 24 px, and keep AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) in the head. Batch 1536 with drop_last at all three shapes. Capture and warm up a third CUDA graph (28 px) in build so nothing recompiles in the timed region. Log per-phase ms/step.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy +0.1 to +0.25 pp, to about 0.756-0.758. Weaker regularization should let the short, under-trained low-res phase fit faster, while the full-res phase still applies ls 0.3. Since the E020/E021 trajectory noise is ~0.15-0.2 pp, only a gain >=0.2 pp counts as support. In that case, spend it on -0.25 full-res epoch (about -0.2 s). A drop of >=0.15 pp refutes the per-phase-regularization idea here.
description: Explore, following C0012 (EfficientNetV2: scale regularization with image size). On E021 at a fixed epoch schedule, weaken regularization only in the 24 px phase. Use label smoothing 0.2 instead of 0.3 and crop translation of 1 px instead of 2, applied before downscaling, during epochs 1-5. The 32 px phase stays at ls 0.3 and 2 px translate. Pass the ls value through the CUDA graph as a GPU scalar tensor, or capture the low-res graph with its own constant, so nothing is recaptured in the timed region. Time should be unchanged.

expected: Per-step time -8 to -10% in both phases (as E009's 9%), so time is about 7.62 x 0.91 + 0.42 = about 7.3-7.45 s (-2 to -4%). Accuracy 0.7505-0.757: a -0.3 to -0.7 pp cut cost, larger than E009's because no 16x16 conv remains, offset by about +0.45 pp from the extra half epoch. It wins only if it is >=0.7535 at <=7.5 s. The profiler should show >=40% of GPU time in non-conv kernels at 32x32/16x16; if it shows <30%, H2.4's memory-bandwidth mechanism is weakened.
description: Exploit, rebasing the next group-1 cut onto the resizing incumbent. On E021, reduce group 1 from 2 convs to 1: keep the 32x32 whitening-output -> 128 conv followed by pool/BN/GELU, and remove the remaining 16x16 128->128 conv with its BN/GELU. Add 0.5 epoch at 32 px (5x24 + 6.25x32) to compensate. Recapture both graphs in build. In the smoke test, also record a one-step torch.profiler breakdown per stage: conv kernels vs BN/activation/pool kernels, at both 24 and 32 px. This tests H2.4.1.
note: Settled by E023: the same 1/3/3 cut on E021 with +0.75 epoch (more compensation than I032's +0.5) gave 0.7484 @ 7.60 s, infeasible and not faster; the cut costs ~1.4 pp for -7% per step.

expected: Time unchanged (±1%). 3-seed mean in 0.753-0.758. A |delta| >=0.2 pp means sub-0.2 pp effects (A28 px stage, NS-step cut, ls per phase) must be treated as inconclusive, and a >=0.755 margin is required before keeping a time cut. If |delta| <=0.1 pp, 0.7535 is an acceptable keep bar. If the salted mean is <0.753, the incumbent's feasibility is fragile and the next kept change must add margin.
description: Noise calibration on the current incumbent, with no recipe change. Add an internal salt to the data-order/augmentation generator (the trial seeds stay 0, 1, 2) and run E021 with salt=1. Compare against E021's 0.7552 (salt 0) and log per-seed accuracies. This replaces I028, which was calibrated on E018, now superseded. The margin on the current tip (+0.22 pp) is the binding constraint for every remaining time cut.

expected: Time +0 to +0.5% (one fused foreach op). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.3 pp, with a weak prior toward +0.1 to +0.2 pp, because the effective step size no longer shrinks as filter norms grow. If the gain is >=0.2 pp, keep it and trade it for -0.25 full-res epoch. If the drop is >=0.2 pp, the norm growth is doing useful implicit LR decay alongside the triangle; close this component of H1.7.
description: Explore an untested H1.7 component: airbench94_muon's per-step weight renormalization. On E021, after each Muon update, rescale every Muon-managed conv weight so each output filter's norm stays at its value at init (or at sqrt(fan_in)-scaled unit norm, as in airbench94_muon). This keeps the effective LR constant under BN scale-invariance. Implement it as one foreach norm/mul inside the CUDA-graphed step and keep weight decay on the Muon group unchanged. Keep lr 0.205, momentum 0.655, Lookahead, the triangle and the resolution schedule fixed.
note: Premise wrong: the incumbent's Muon already renormalizes each conv weight every step (p *= sqrt(out_channels)/||p||, the airbench94_muon rule) inside the CUDA-graphed update; only a per-filter variant would be new.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, about 7.34 s). 2-salt mean accuracy +0.1 to +0.3 pp over the pooled 0.7533, i.e. about 0.7545-0.7565. If the 2-salt mean is >=0.7553 (+0.2 pp), keep it: that margin pays for the next time cuts. If it is <=0.7513, the lr was already high: run 0.8x (0.164) next. If it falls in between, the result is inconclusive; close the lr axis.
description: Exploit and add margin. On the E025 incumbent (5x24 + 2x28 + 4x32 px, 2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with momentum 0.655, Turbo preconditioning plus 2 NS steps, CUDA graphs per resolution, Lookahead and triangle), raise the Muon peak lr by 1.25x, from 0.205 to 0.256, and change nothing else. The SGD groups, momentum, schedule shape and resolution schedule stay fixed. The LR lives in the GPU schedule tensor, so the graphs need no recapture. Rationale: the E024 note says Turbo preconditioning shrank the effective update on the big layers by about 1/3, and the inherited Hiverge lr was tuned for a 3/3/3 CIFAR-10 net without resizing. Run salt 0 (official) and also salt 1, so the comparison is against the pooled E025/E027 estimate of 0.7533 and not E025's single draw of 0.7539.

expected: 28/32 px ms/step falls 2-4%, so total time falls 1-2% (about -0.08 to -0.15 s, to about 7.2-7.27 s). This is work removed, so it should carry over to the PCIe judge (H5.1). Accuracy within ±0.15 pp of the pooled 0.7533, since airbench also freezes the whitening bias after about 3 epochs. Keep it if the 3-seed mean is >=0.753 and time is >=1% lower. If accuracy falls by >=0.25 pp, the whitening bias needs the full-res phase; refute H2.4.4.
description: Exploit by removing high-resolution backward work that carries little accuracy. On E025, train the whitening-conv bias only during the 24 px phase (epochs 1-5). In the 28 px and 32 px phases, detach the whitening-layer output (after its activation) before group 1. Autograd then skips the dgrad of the first 128-channel conv and the whitening BN/activation backward at the highest resolutions. In the optimizer, drop the whitening bias from those phases' parameter list, or zero its LR. The 28 and 32 px graphs are captured in build with the detach already in place, and the 24 px graph is unchanged, so no new graph count and no recapture in the timed region. Log per-phase ms/step.

expected: A 20 px epoch costs about 0.40-0.44 s versus about 0.54 s at 24 px, so time falls about 0.2-0.28 s (-3 to -4%, to about 7.06-7.14 s). Accuracy falls 0.05-0.3 pp, centred near -0.15 pp (about 0.752 expected). If the 3-seed mean is >=0.753, keep it. If it falls between 0.750 and 0.753, combine it with any free margin gain (the Muon lr idea) or add +0.25 epoch at 32 px; the net should still be about -0.1 s. If it falls below 0.750, the low-res floor is 24 px.
description: Exploit the resolution ladder one rung lower. On E025, run epochs 1-2 at 20 px instead of 24 px, so the schedule becomes 2x20 + 3x24 + 2x28 + 4x32 (11 epochs in total, the same LR schedule over total steps). Use whole augmented images downscaled with bilinear F.interpolate after the 2 px translate crop, as for 24/28 px, and keep the AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) head. Batch 1536 with drop_last. Capture and warm up a 4th CUDA graph (20 px) in build. Rationale: the first epochs learn coarse features and the triangle is still warming up, so resolution matters least there. E020 and E025 both gained from cheaper early pixels.

expected: About 80 fewer optimizer steps, and the 24 px convs run at a larger, more efficient batch. Low-res phase time falls 8-12%, so total time falls 2-4% (about -0.15 to -0.25 s). Accuracy falls 0.05-0.3 pp: E017 and E022 show that fewer steps cost some accuracy, though less in the under-fit early phase. Keep it if the 3-seed mean is >=0.753 and time is >=2% lower. If accuracy falls by >=0.3 pp, early-phase step count matters; refute H2.3.3.
description: Explore cutting the fixed per-step cost (Muon ~1.5 ms/step after E024, plus Lookahead and launch costs) in the cheap low-res phase. On E025, use batch 3072 in the 24 px phase only (epochs 1-5, 16 steps/epoch with drop_last instead of 32). In that phase, scale the Muon lr by sqrt(2) (0.29) and the SGD-group lr linearly (2x), with momentum unchanged. Keep batch 1536 at 28 and 32 px. Define the LR schedule per step over the new total step count, keeping the same epoch boundaries. Capture the 24 px graph at batch 3072 in build (one graph per resolution, as now).

expected: Time +0.42 s (about 7.76 s). Accuracy +0.35 to +0.6 pp over the pooled 0.7533, i.e. about 0.757-0.759. This gives a slope of 0.8-1.4 pp/s. It will not beat E025 on time, so log it as calibration (discard). If the gain is <0.25 pp, the 32 px tail is saturating: per-step cuts are worth less than assumed, and future margin should come from schedule or lr changes rather than epochs.
description: Measure the exchange rate and build a safe-margin fallback. On E025, add 0.5 epoch at 32 px (5x24 + 2x28 + 4.5x32, LR schedule over total steps) and change nothing else. A 0.5-epoch step is about 2x the measured trajectory noise, so unlike the 0.25-epoch trim of E021 its effect can be read. The result fixes the pp/s line against which E024-style cuts and the 20 px and batch ideas are scored. It also gives the config to fall back on if the official 40-seed mean of E025 looks marginal (pooled 0.7533).

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.15 to +0.25 pp, with a weak prior near +0.1 pp (about 0.7543). Keep it only if the 3-seed mean is >=0.7553 (+0.2 pp over the pooled 0.7533). In that case spend the gain on the 20 px start. A drop of >=0.15 pp closes the ls axis at 0.3.
description: Explore the last untested direction of the label-smoothing knob on the current recipe. On E025, raise label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.4 in all phases, and change nothing else. ls is a constant in the loss, so recapture the graphs in build. Rationale: E012 (0.3 to 0.2 lost 0.21 pp) shows that more output regularization helped. With 100 classes and an under-fit, heavily augmented 11-epoch schedule, the optimum may sit above 0.3.
note: ideate: Based on E025, which is superseded by E030. It is re-queued unchanged (ls 0.4) on E030, with the keep bar raised to 0.755 because the expected accuracy of the incumbent is about at the 0.753 bar.

expected: 32 px ms/step falls 5-9%, so total time falls about 0.15-0.25 s (-2 to -3.5%), to about 6.7-6.8 s. Accuracy -0.0 to -0.3 pp versus the pooled ~0.753, centred near -0.1 pp. Keep it if the 3-seed mean is >=0.753 and time is >=1.5% lower; also run a salt-1 companion if it lands within 0.1 pp of the bar. If accuracy falls >=0.3 pp, conv1 still needs full-res updates: try freezing only during the last 2 epochs.
description: Exploit: remove more high-resolution backward work, extending E029. On E030 (2x20+3x24+2x28+4x32 px, 0.7533 @ 6.95 s), freeze the whole first group-1 conv block (conv 32x32 whitening-output -> 128, pool, BN, GELU) during the 4 epochs at 32 px. In the 32 px CUDA graph, detach the block's output before the second group-1 conv, and drop that conv's weight and its BN affine params from that phase's Muon/SGD parameter lists (or zero their LR). E029 already skips this conv's dgrad. This change also removes its wgrad at 32x32 and the BN/GELU/pool backward at 32x32 and 16x16. BN stays in train mode, so running stats keep updating at 32 px. Capture the modified 32 px graph in build, keeping the same graph count with no recapture in the timed region. Log ms/step per phase. Rationale (FreezeOut-style): the first conv sees the whitened patches and converges earliest. The 28 px and 20/24 px phases (7 epochs) still train it.

expected: Muon time drops about 0.2-0.3 ms/step, so time falls about 0.07-0.1 s (-1 to -1.5%), to about 6.85-6.88 s. Accuracy within ±0.2 pp of the pooled ~0.753. Keep it if the 3-seed mean is >=0.753 and time is >=0.8% lower. If accuracy falls >=0.3 pp, 2 NS steps is the floor; close the NS-step axis for H2.5.2.
description: Exploit: cut Muon's fixed per-step cost (about 1.5 ms of ~350 steps, roughly 7% of train time) once more. On E030, keep Turbo/AOL column preconditioning but run 1 Newton-Schulz quintic step instead of 2. Use the same coefficients, the same lr 0.205, momentum 0.655, and the per-step weight renorm unchanged. Recapture all 4 graphs in build. Rationale: E024 showed Muon is insensitive to singular-value spread in [0.67, 1.2], and E028 showed accuracy is flat in lr over 0.205-0.256. The per-step renorm also fixes the overall update scale, so a less exact orthogonalization may cost nothing. Log Muon ms/step.

expected: Time +0.40-0.43 s (about 7.36 s). Accuracy +0.35 to +0.6 pp, about 0.757-0.759, a slope of 0.8-1.4 pp/s. This won't beat E030 on time, so log it as calibration (discard). If the gain is <0.25 pp, the 32 px tail is saturating; margin must then come from lr/schedule, and per-step cuts are worth less than assumed.
description: Rebase of I039 onto the current incumbent, for calibration and a safe-margin fallback. On E030, add 0.5 epoch at 32 px (2x20+3x24+2x28+4.5x32, LR triangle and Lookahead over total steps) and change nothing else. A 0.5-epoch step is about 2x the trajectory noise, so its effect can be read. It fixes the pp/s line at the 32 px end for scoring per-step cuts. It also gives the config to submit if the official 40-seed mean of E030 looks marginal.
note: Already run as E032 (I039 applied to E030): +0.5 epoch at 32 px on E030 gave 0.7527 @ 7.34 s, i.e. no measurable gain.

expected: Time +0.42-0.45 s (about 7.38 s). Accuracy +0.15 to +0.5 pp, centred near +0.3 pp. If its gain is >= the +0.5 epoch at 32 px run (I039 rebased) at equal time, low-res epochs are the cheaper margin source: future margin top-ups should be low-res epochs, and the 32 px phase can be trimmed (see the 28 px shift idea). If the gain is <0.15 pp, early epochs are saturated and margin must come from the 32 px end.
description: Explore which pixels buy margin most cheaply, as a companion to the rebased I039. On E030, add one extra 20 px epoch at the start (3x20+3x24+2x28+4x32, 12 epochs, LR triangle and Lookahead over total steps; same 20 px graph, no new shapes). Change nothing else. The 20 px epoch is the cheapest epoch (~0.43 s), and E031 showed that early-phase optimizer step count matters under Muon. So extra early steps may buy as much accuracy per second as the 32 px tail at roughly equal cost.

expected: Time -0.17 to -0.2 s (a 28 px epoch costs ~0.66 s vs ~0.84 s at 32 px), to about 6.75-6.8 s (-2.5%). Accuracy -0.0 to -0.25 pp, centred near -0.1 pp. Keep it if the 2-salt mean is >=0.753. If the loss is <=0.1 pp, H2.3.2 is supported and a 2x32 px tail is next. If the loss is >=0.3 pp, the 32 px phase is doing feature learning, not just BN re-fitting; refute H2.3.2.
description: Exploit and test the FixRes mechanism: the closing full-res phase only needs to re-fit BN stats and the head, so it can be shorter. On the current incumbent (E030, or the low-res-epoch variant if that run is kept), move one 32 px epoch to 28 px: 2x20+3x24+3x28+3x32 (11 epochs, same LR schedule over total steps, same 4 graphs). Change nothing else. Run salt 0 and salt 1 and compare against the pooled estimate, since the expected effect is near the noise.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.15 to +0.25 pp, weak prior near +0.1 pp. Keep it only if the 3-seed mean is >=0.755 (+0.2 pp over the pooled ~0.753), then spend the margin on a time cut (freeze conv1, 28 px shift). A drop of >=0.15 pp closes the ls axis at 0.3.
description: Rebase of I040 onto the current incumbent. On E030, raise label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.4 in all phases and change nothing else. ls is a graph constant, so recapture all 4 graphs in build. E012 (0.3 -> 0.2 lost 0.21 pp) suggests the optimum may sit at or above 0.3 for 100 classes in an under-fit 11-epoch schedule. This is the last untested direction of the ls knob, and it is time-free.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.25 to +0.3 pp, no strong prior. Keep it if the 3-seed mean is >=0.755 (a salt-1 companion is required if it lands in 0.753-0.755). If it falls >=0.2 pp, try 0.55 next only if the drop is large (>=0.4 pp); otherwise close the momentum axis.
description: Explore an untested Muon knob: momentum. E028 showed lr is flat over 0.205-0.256, but momentum 0.655 is inherited from Hiverge's CIFAR-10 3/3/3 net without resizing or AOL. On E030, raise the Muon momentum from 0.655 to 0.75 (Nesterov form unchanged) and keep lr, the SGD groups, the schedule, Lookahead and resolutions fixed. Momentum is a graph constant, so recapture all graphs in build. Rationale: E031 showed the early phase is step-limited; higher momentum smooths the orthogonalized direction across consecutive small-batch steps, which may raise per-step progress.

expected: Time falls 0.5-1.5% (about 6.59-6.65 s vs 6.68 s), because the atomic scatter in the adaptive-max backward is gone at all 4 resolutions. Accuracy should be bit-identical or within ±0.05 pp of 0.7546; only fp16 tie-breaking in the gradient can differ. Keep if time is >=0.5% lower and the 3-seed mean is >=0.753. If time changes by <0.3%, the pooling backward is not a measurable cost, H2.6.1 is refuted and H2.6's kernel-efficiency lever drops in confidence. This is removed work, so it should carry over to the PCIe judge.
description: Exploit, a numerically equivalent throughput cut. On the current tip (E038: 2x20+3x24+2x28+4x32 px, 2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with AOL plus 2 NS steps, conv1 block frozen at 32 px, ls 0.4; 0.7546 @ 6.68 s), replace the head's AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).amax(2), or an equivalent amax over dims (2,3), in every resolution's forward. Change nothing else. Recapture all 4 CUDA graphs and the eval path in build. Confirm that eval still returns finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. In the smoke test, log ms/step per phase and a one-step profiler line for the pooling backward kernel (atomic adaptive_max_pool2d_backward vs the amax backward).
note: E041 crashed: fix and relaunch, or drop it

expected: Time rises by 0.04-0.07 s (+0.6-1%, about 6.73-6.75 s). The 2-salt mean rises 0.05-0.3 pp over the tip's 0.7527, centred near +0.15 pp (about 0.754). Keep it if the 2-salt mean is >=0.7545 and salt 0 is >=0.753; that margin then pays for the E037-style 28 px shift (-0.10 s) or extending the freeze to 28 px. If the gain is <0.05 pp, the running stats already match the slow weights: refute the BN-mismatch part of H2.3.2 and close the BN-stat lever.
description: Exploit and add margin by fixing a BN-statistics mismatch (D004 C0031/C0035). Lookahead copies the slow weights into the model at the end of training, but the BN running statistics were accumulated under the fast iterates, and the frozen block's stats under the detach regime. At the end of train(), after the final Lookahead sync, reset all BN running stats. Re-estimate them with cumulative averaging (momentum=None) from 6 forward-only batches of 1536 un-augmented, un-flipped 32 px training images (no_grad, fp16, channels_last). Draw the images with the trial-seeded generator, then restore BN momentum. Do the re-estimation pass in a small CUDA graph or compiled function warmed up in build on synthetic data, so its first call costs nothing extra in the timed region. Training data only; the test set is never touched. Change nothing else on E038. Run salt 0 and salt 1.

expected: Time +3-6% (about 6.9-7.05 s): group 3 runs at 4x4 to 2.5x2.5, where E004 measured only +6%/step for +19% MACs, and the low-res phases add less. The 2-salt mean rises 0.15-0.45 pp over 0.7527, centred near +0.3 pp (about 0.7555). H6.1.1 is supported if the gain is >=0.3 pp for <=+5% time. In that case keep it, and spend the margin next on the 28 px shift (E037: -0.10 s) and the 28 px freeze (H2.4.6), which together should more than repay the time. If the gain is <0.15 pp, H6.1 is weakened and H6's capacity route is closed for group 3.
description: Exploit and buy margin through cheap deep capacity, at equal epochs (the test E008 confounded). On E038, widen group 3 from 576 to 768 channels (128/384/768) at every resolution and adjust the head input to match. Keep epochs, resolution schedule, LR schedule, Muon lr/momentum, ls 0.4, freezing and the whitening-bias window fixed. Recapture all 4 graphs in build. Log ms/step per phase. Run salt 0 and salt 1.

expected: 20/24 px ms/step falls 3-6%, so total time falls 1-2% (about 6.55-6.62 s). Accuracy within ±0.15 pp of the tip (E029 found 3 vs 5 epochs of bias training neutral). Keep if the 3-seed mean is >=0.753 and time is >=1% lower; run a salt-1 companion if salt 0 lands in 0.753-0.7545. If accuracy falls >=0.25 pp, the whitening bias needs the early phase; refute H2.4.5.
description: Exploit, removing low-res backward work. On E038, train the whitening-conv bias for only the first ~0.25 epoch (8 steps at batch 1536), as Fable and Hiverge do, instead of the first 5 epochs. After that, detach the whitening output (after its activation) in every phase, including 20 and 24 px. The 20/24 px phases then also skip the first group-1 conv's dgrad and the whitening BN/activation backward. Capture a no-detach 20 px graph for the first 8 steps plus the detached 20/24 px graphs in build, so nothing is captured in the timed region (5 graphs in total). Drop the whitening bias from the optimizer, or zero its lr, after step 8. Change nothing else.

expected: Time unchanged (about 6.68 s per trial). 10-seed mean in [0.7500, 0.7535], centred near 0.752, below the kept 0.7546, with a per-seed std of 0.15-0.4 pp. If the mean is <0.7525, enforce the H4 rule: no numerics-changing time cut is kept until a margin-adding change (BN re-estimation, group-3 width) passes with 2 salts. Only bit-identical cuts (amax pooling) stay allowed. If the mean is >=0.753, salt 0 is representative, and single-draw keeps at >=0.7535 are acceptable again.
description: Calibration (no recipe change), to set the keep rule. Using the existing internal salt / trial-seed plumbing, run the E038 tip recipe on dev seeds 3-12 outside the official command (10 trials, same code), and log per-seed accuracy and time. Nothing is kept from this run. The result replaces the 2-salt guesses with a 10-seed estimate of the recipe's true mean and per-seed std, and tests whether official seeds 0-2 are a favourable draw: salt-1 draws came in lower three times (E027, E034, E039).

expected: 32 px ms/step falls 1.5-3%, so total time falls 0.7-1.5% (about 6.59-6.64 s). Accuracy within ±0.15 pp: the block is frozen and its output distribution becomes deterministic per image, which may even reduce train/test mismatch. Keep if the 3-seed mean is >=0.753 and time is >=0.7% lower. If accuracy drops >=0.25 pp, the batch-stat noise in that block acts as useful regularization at 32 px; refute H2.6.2.
description: Exploit, a kernel-efficiency cut in the most expensive phase. On E038, during the 4 epochs at 32 px, switch the frozen first group-1 block's BatchNorm to eval mode: it uses fixed running stats, gets no batch-stat reductions and no stat updates. Before entering the 32 px phase, re-estimate that one BN's running stats from 2 forward-only 32 px training batches (cumulative average), so its fixed affine matches the 32 px input distribution. Fold it into a per-channel scale/shift fused after the conv if inductor allows. Capture the modified 32 px graph and the tiny re-estimation pass in build. Change nothing else.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). The 2-salt mean rises 0.0-0.25 pp over 0.7527, centred near +0.1 pp. Keep if the 2-salt mean is >=0.7545. If it rises >=0.15 pp, the orthogonalization quality on the small-singular-value tail is a margin lever, and 2-step PE may later make room for other cuts. If it changes by <0.1 pp, orthogonalization quality past 2 AOL+NS steps is saturated; close H1.7.9.
description: Explore a margin source inside Muon at no time cost. On E038, replace the 2 fixed quintic NS steps that follow AOL preconditioning with Polar Express per-iteration minimax coefficients for 2 iterations (arXiv 2505.16932), with the lower singular-value bound set to ~1e-3 and the safety factor from the paper. AOL already bounds sigma_max <= 1. Use the same matmul count, the same lr 0.205, momentum 0.655 and per-step renorm. Before running, validate offline on 3 real momentum-gradient matrices captured from a dev training step (not Gaussian; the E035 lesson) that the smallest decile of singular values is lifted higher than with the current coefficients. Recapture all graphs in build. Run salt 0 and salt 1.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). The 2-salt mean moves by -0.3 to +0.3 pp with no strong prior; the scale changes both the head's effective lr and the logit-margin target under ls 0.4. Keep if the 2-salt mean is >=0.7545. A |delta| >=0.15 pp in either direction supports H1.3.4 and sets the direction for the next run. A |delta| <0.1 pp refutes H1.3.4 and closes the output-regularization knobs (ls and scale) as margin sources.
description: Explore an output knob that has never been swept and costs nothing. On E038 (ls 0.4), multiply the head's fixed output scale (the airbench 1/9-style logit multiplier, rescaled for 100 classes) by 2x and change nothing else. The scale is a graph constant, so recapture all graphs in build. Run salt 0 and salt 1. Contingency: if the 2-salt mean falls by >=0.15 pp, run 0.5x next. Larger smoothing (ls 0.4) lowers the optimal logit magnitude, so the scale and ls interact.

expected: Time about 6.52-6.58 s, down 1.5-2.4% from 6.68 s: -0.19 s from pooling and +0.04-0.05 s for 4 re-estimation batches. Official 3-seed accuracy 0.7525-0.757. Dev 10-seed mean 0.7535-0.7555, centred near +0.1 pp over 0.7534. Keep if official >=0.7535 and dev mean >=0.753. A dev gain >=0.1 pp supports the BN-mismatch part of H2.3.2 and makes this the margin base for the 28 px freeze and bias-window cuts. A dev gain <0.03 pp refutes it: then drop the re-estimation and re-apply the pooling cut alone with the next margin source.
description: Exploit by stacking two near-misses. On E038 (2x20+3x24+2x28+4x32 px, 2/3/3, Muon with AOL plus 2 NS steps, conv1 block frozen at 32 px, ls 0.4; 6.68 s), make two changes. (1) Re-apply E042's pooling cut: replace the head's AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).max(dim=2).values at every resolution and in eval. Use the indices-based backward, not amax, because amax crashed in E041. (2) Add E043's end-of-train BN re-estimation with 4 batches instead of 6. After the final Lookahead sync, reset all BN running stats. Re-estimate them with momentum=None from 4 forward-only batches of 1536 un-augmented 32 px training images, drawn with the trial-seeded generator, under no_grad, fp16 and channels_last. Then restore BN momentum. Put the re-estimation pass in a small graph or compiled function warmed up in build on synthetic data. Recapture all 4 train graphs in build. Check that eval gives finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. Besides the official run, evaluate the same code on dev seeds 3-12 outside the official command, so the BN-re-estimation gain is measured against E046's 10-seed baseline of 0.7534 with SE about 0.09 pp, not against a single draw.

expected: 24 px ms/step falls about 3-5%, so total time falls about 0.04-0.07 s (-0.6 to -1%). This is removed work, so it should carry over to the PCIe judge. Dev 10-seed mean within ±0.1 pp of the base. Keep if official >=0.7535, dev mean >=0.753 and time is >=0.5% lower. If the dev mean falls by >=0.2 pp, the bias needs the 24 px phase. Then the window lies between 2 and 3 epochs and H2.4.8 is closed as not worth a graph.
description: Exploit, removing low-res backward work at a phase boundary, so no new graph is needed. On the current tip (idea A's stack if kept, else E038 plus the pooling cut), train the whitening-conv bias only during the 20 px phase (epochs 1-2, about 64 steps) instead of epochs 1-5. In the 24 px phase, detach the whitening output (after its activation) before group 1, as the 28/32 px graphs already do, and zero the whitening bias lr or drop it from that phase's parameter list. The 24 px graph is recaptured in build with the detach. The 20 px graph is unchanged and the graph count stays 4. This is the 2-epoch window between E045's 8 steps (failed, -0.47 pp) and E029's 3 epochs (neutral), aligned with the 20->24 px boundary. Also evaluate dev seeds 3-12. Log ms/step in the 24 px phase.

expected: 28 px ms/step falls 5-8%, so total time falls about 0.07-0.11 s (-1 to -1.7%), to about 6.45-6.5 s if stacked on idea A. Dev 10-seed mean -0.0 to -0.2 pp, centred near -0.08 pp. Keep if official >=0.7535 and dev mean >=0.753 (H2.4.6's base-margin condition). If the dev mean drops by >=0.2 pp, conv1 still needs the near-full-res updates: refute H2.4.6 and keep the freeze at 32 px only.
description: Exploit, extending the FreezeOut-style cut. On the current tip (idea A's stack if kept, else E038 plus the pooling cut), also freeze the first group-1 conv block (whitening-output -> 128 conv, pool, BN, GELU) during the 2 epochs at 28 px, exactly as already done at 32 px. In the 28 px graph, detach the block's output before the second group-1 conv. Drop that conv's weight and BN affine params from the 28 px phase's Muon/SGD lists, or zero their lr. BN stays in train mode. Recapture the 28 px graph in build; the graph count is unchanged. conv1 is then trained only in the 5 epochs at 20/24 px. Evaluate dev seeds 3-12 alongside the official run. Log ms/step per phase.

expected: ms/step +2.5-4%, so time about +0.17-0.25 s over the pooling-cut base (about 6.68-6.75 s; roughly equal to E038 without the pooling cut). Dev 10-seed mean +0.1 to +0.25 pp, centred near +0.17 pp (E044's 768 gave +0.4 pp on one draw). If the dev gain is >=0.2 pp at <=+4% time, H6.1.3 is supported, and this becomes the margin base that the 28 px shift (E037) and the 28 px freeze are spent against. A dev gain <0.1 pp means group-3 capacity is only useful at large widths: close H6.1.
description: Exploit, buying margin through the smallest group-3 capacity step. Before the official run, microbenchmark ms/step per phase on the current recipe (graphed, Muon included) for group-3 widths 576 and 640. Do not reuse E004/E044 deltas: the E044 post-mortem showed that the cost structure has shifted. If 640 costs <=+4% ms/step, then on the current tip (with the pooling cut) widen group 3 from 576 to 640 at every resolution and adjust the head input. Hold epochs, resolutions, LR schedule, Muon lr/momentum, ls, freezing and the bias window fixed. Recapture all graphs in build. Run official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If the microbenchmark shows >+5%, log it and do not run.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Dev 10-seed mean moves -0.3 to +0.3 pp with no strong prior. The multiplier was tuned for Nesterov SGD at batch 1024, lr 9.0, and the SGD groups have since been rescaled linearly for batch 1536. A |delta| >=0.15 pp supports H1.7.12 and sets the direction. Keep if the dev gain is >=0.1 pp and official >=0.7535. A |delta| <0.1 pp closes the SGD-group knobs as margin sources.
description: Explore an SGD-era knob never varied under Muon. Note: with per-step weight renorm, weight decay on the Muon conv group is effectively a no-op, so the live knobs are the SGD-group settings. On E038 (or the current tip), halve the BN-bias lr multiplier from 64x to 32x, and change nothing else. Keep Muon lr/momentum, head lr, wd, the schedule and Lookahead fixed. The multiplier lives in the per-group lr. If it is folded into the GPU schedule tensor, no recapture is needed; otherwise recapture in build. Evaluate dev seeds 3-12 plus official seeds. Contingency: if the dev mean falls by >=0.15 pp, run 128x next.

expected: Time about 6.42-6.46 s (-3.3 to -3.9%: pooling -0.19 s, bias window -0.06 s; E049 measured 6.45 s for the same pair). Both cuts remove work, so the gain should carry over to the PCIe judge. Dev 10-seed mean about 0.7565 (range 0.754-0.759): the cuts measured -0.09 and -0.04 pp on dev, against E053's 0.7578. Keep if official >=0.7535 and dev >=0.754. If dev falls >=0.25 pp below E053, the scale-2x gain interacts with the max-pool gradient routing; then re-test the pooling cut alone.
description: Exploit: spend E053's margin on the two time cuts already measured as accuracy-neutral on dev seeds. On E053 (E038 + head output scale 2x, ls 0.4; official 0.7575, dev 0.7578 @ 6.68 s), make two changes. (1) The pooling cut: replace the head's AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).max(dim=2).values at every resolution and in eval. Use the indices-based backward, not amax (amax crashed in E041). (2) E049's 2-epoch whitening-bias window: train the whitening-conv bias only in the 20 px phase, and in the 24 px graph detach the whitening output after its activation and zero the bias lr. Keep the graph count at 4, recapture everything in build, and change nothing else. Check that eval returns finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12.

expected: Time -0.09 to -0.11 s (E037 measured -0.10 s), about 6.33-6.36 s on A's stack. Dev mean -0.0 to -0.25 pp vs the tip, centred near -0.1 pp. Keep if dev >=0.754 and official >=0.7535. A dev drop <=0.1 pp supports H2.3.2 (the closing 32 px phase mostly re-fits to the test resolution), and 2x28+... toward a 2x32 tail becomes the next probe. A drop >=0.3 pp means the 32 px phase is doing feature learning: refute H2.3.2 and close the ladder.
description: Exploit, the next banked cut, stacked on the current tip (idea A's stack if kept, else E053). Move one 32 px epoch to 28 px, giving 2x20+3x24+3x28+3x32: 11 epochs, the LR triangle and Lookahead over total steps, the same 4 graphs. The 28 px graph keeps conv1 trainable, as now (E050 showed conv1 needs its 28 px updates). Change nothing else. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12, and compare against the tip's own dev mean.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Dev mean -0.3 to +0.3 pp vs the tip, weak prior +0.05 to +0.15 pp: 1x→2x gave +0.44 pp, so the optimum likely sits at or above 2x but the response must flatten. Keep if dev gain >=0.1 pp and official >=0.7535. A gain would add margin to spend on the tail trim and group-2 cut.
description: Explore, continuing the only margin source found since E030. On the current tip (A's stack if kept, else E053), raise the head's fixed output scale from 2x to 3x the original airbench-derived value. ls stays 0.4 and nothing else changes. The scale is a graph constant, so recapture all graphs in build. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. Contingency: if dev rises >=0.15 pp, try 4x next. If it falls >=0.15 pp, 2x is near the optimum; then test ls 0.3 at 2x scale, since the scale and ls interact.

expected: Time -0.32 to -0.38 s (about -5%). Dev mean -0.1 to -0.45 pp vs the tip, centred near -0.25 pp. Keep if dev >=0.754 and official >=0.7535; the -5% would beat any other banked cut. A dev drop <=0.15 pp means the 32 px tail is saturated (the H6/plateau reading gains, and margin should go to tail trims). A drop >=0.4 pp means the tail is ~1 pp/epoch: stop trimming epochs and spend margin only on per-step cuts.
description: Exploit, and measure the tail slope in the cheap direction now that margin exists. On the current tip, cut the 32 px phase from 4 to 3.5 epochs (16 fewer steps at batch 1536 with drop_last). Keep the LR triangle and Lookahead over total steps, as in E032, which added the same half-epoch. Change nothing else; no new graphs. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. E032's +0.5 epoch at 32 px bought -0.06 pp on one draw, so the tail may be saturated and a trim could be cheap.

expected: Time -3 to -5% (about -0.2 to -0.3 s), including Muon NS savings from one fewer 384x3456 filter matrix. Dev mean -0.15 to -0.6 pp, centred near -0.3 pp (group-1's first depth cut cost 0.29 pp in E009). Keep if dev >=0.754 and official >=0.7535. If the cost is <=0.3 pp for >=4% time, this beats the epoch line, and H6.1.4 (2 convs at 512) becomes the follow-up to buy the accuracy back.
description: Exploit, a work-removal cut in group 2 that has not yet been tried. First microbenchmark ms/step per phase on the current recipe (graphed, Muon included) for group 2 at 3 vs 2 convs. If the 2-conv version saves >=3% ms/step, cut group 2 from 3 convs to 2 (net 2/2/3) at the same width 384, keeping the pooling position, and adjust the Muon batched-NS shape groups. Hold epochs, resolutions, schedule, ls, head scale, freezing and the bias window fixed. Recapture all graphs in build. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If the microbenchmark saves <2%, log it and do not run.

expected: Metrics unchanged (no submission change). Prediction: tip train accuracy in [0.82, 0.92], train-test gap <=15 pp, and the 2x scale raises train accuracy by at least its +0.44 pp test gain. Train accuracy >=0.95 refutes H7.1 and moves margin work to regularization (jitter H1.3.5, flip H1.2, ls form). Train accuracy <0.85 supports capacity and anchor-fixed steps (H1.8.2, H6.1).
description: Explore, a diagnostic only, run outside the official command and the timed region, with no recipe change. After training on dev seeds 3-7 (5 trials), compute un-augmented top-1 accuracy and mean loss on a fixed 10k training subset (drawn with a fixed generator) for two configs: the current tip and E038 (head scale 1x). Test accuracy is logged as usual. Nothing is kept. This tells us whether the head-scale gain came from better fit or less over-regularization, and whether the recipe under-fits (margin from steps or capacity) or has a large gap (margin from regularization).

expected: Muon GPU time -0.1 to -0.2 ms/step over about 350 steps, so time -0.04 to -0.07 s (-0.6 to -1%). Dev mean within ±0.1 pp of the tip (same math up to fp16 rounding). Keep if time is >=0.5% lower, dev >=0.754 and official >=0.7535. This is removed FLOPs, so it should carry over to the judge.
description: Exploit, numerically near-equivalent work removal in Muon. First check the AOL code. If the column scaling computes X^T X and the first NS step then recomputes the Gram matrix, reuse it as A1 = s·A0·s (Turbo-Muon Algorithm 2), removing one large matmul per parameter group per step inside the batched NS call. If the reuse is already present, close H2.5.5 without a run. Otherwise change nothing else, recapture all graphs in build, and run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12.
note: Already implemented since E024: the AOL preconditioning computes A = X X^T on the small side, rescales it to D A D and reuses it as the first NS step's Gram matrix (no extra matmul).

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, about 5.25 s). Dev mean between -0.25 and +0.3 pp of 0.7557, with a weak prior of +0.05 to +0.15 pp: 64x to 32x gave +0.27 pp, and the response should flatten. Keep if dev gains >=0.1 pp and official >=0.7535. That margin would pay for the group-3 depth cut.
description: Exploit, a time-free margin source and the pre-registered follow-up to E054. On the E059 tip (2/2/3 net, 2x20+3x24+3x28+2.5x32 px, head scale 2x, ls 0.4, BN-bias lr multiplier 32x; official 0.7565, dev 0.7557 @ 5.25 s), halve the BN-bias lr multiplier again, from 32x to 16x, and change nothing else. Muon lr/momentum, head lr, SGD-group wd and momentum, schedule, Lookahead, resolutions, freezing and the bias window all stay fixed. If the multiplier is folded into the GPU schedule tensor, nothing needs recapturing; otherwise recapture all graphs in build. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12 and compare against E059's own dev mean (0.7557). Contingency: if dev rises >=0.15 pp, try 8x next; if it falls >=0.15 pp, 32x is near the optimum and the BN-bias axis is closed.

expected: Time -0.35 to -0.55 s (-7 to -10%, to about 4.7-4.9 s). The group-3 conv has about half the MACs of the removed group-2 conv, but it runs at low efficiency at 4x4 and also drops the biggest NS matmul. Dev mean -0.15 to -0.5 pp, centred near -0.3 pp, so about 0.6-1.2 s per pp, a better trade than the 32 px tail (0.67 pp/s). Keep if dev >=0.754 and official >=0.7535. If dev lands in 0.752-0.754, bank it as a cut to stack with the next margin source (group-2 width).
description: Exploit, work removal in group 3, extending E059's finding that one 8x8 group-2 conv cost ~0.73 s for only -0.15 pp. First microbenchmark ms/step per phase on the current recipe (graphed, Muon included) for group 3 at 3 vs 2 convs. If the 2-conv version saves >=4%, cut group 3 from 3 convs to 2 (net 2/2/2, airbench94-style) at width 576, keeping the pooling position and head. Remove the 576x5184 matrix from the batched-NS shape groups; it is the largest Muon matrix. Hold epochs, resolutions, schedule, ls, head scale, BN-bias multiplier, freezing and the bias window fixed. Recapture all graphs in build. Check that eval returns finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If the microbenchmark saves <3%, log it and do not run. Run this after the BN-bias 16x idea, on whichever base is then the tip.

expected: Time +2.5-5% (about +0.13-0.26 s, to about 5.4-5.5 s). Dev mean +0.1 to +0.3 pp, centred near +0.15 pp. Not keepable on its own (slower). It wins as a margin source if the gain is >=0.67 pp/s (the tail rate), i.e. about >=0.12 pp per +0.18 s. Then it becomes the base for the group-3 depth cut or a further 32 px tail trim. A gain <0.08 pp closes group-2 width as a margin source.
description: Exploit, buying back group-2 capacity after E059's depth cut (depth-for-width). First microbenchmark ms/step per phase for group 2 at 2 convs with width 384 vs 448 (graphed, Muon included). If 448 costs <=+5% ms/step, widen group 2 on the E059 tip from 384 to 448 channels in both of its convs, adjusting the group-3 input conv and the Muon NS shape groups. Hold epochs, resolutions, schedule, ls, head scale, freezing and the bias window fixed. Recapture all graphs in build. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If the microbenchmark shows >+6%, log it and do not run.
note: Settled by its own gate: microbenchmark (dev seeds 3-4) of group 2 at 448 channels gave 5.98 s vs ~5.27 s at 384 (+13.6% per trial), far above the +5% threshold the idea set for running.

expected: Time +0.28-0.34 s (a 20 px epoch on the 2/2/3 net), to about 5.55 s. Dev mean +0.1 to +0.35 pp if anchoring caused E036's loss, i.e. >=0.5 pp/s, comparable to the tail. A dev gain >=0.15 pp supports H1.9 and makes cheap anchored low-res epochs the way to repay structural cuts. A gain <0.05 pp supports the plateau reading (H6) and closes epoch-based margin. Discard as a run unless it also beats the tip on time.
description: Explore whether anchor-fixed low-res steps buy margin, rebased onto the 2/2/3 net, where an epoch is now much cheaper. On the E059 tip, add one 20 px epoch at the start (3x20+3x24+3x28+2.5x32). Fix the LR warmup length and the Lookahead alpha ramp in absolute steps at their E059 values; the decay portion absorbs the extra 32 steps. The whitening bias trains through the whole 20 px phase (3 epochs; E029 found 3-5 epochs neutral), so no new graph is needed. Change nothing else. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. Compare against E036's -0.27 pp, where the anchors moved.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Dev mean -0.2 to +0.25 pp, weak prior +0.05 to +0.1 pp: fixed momentum 0.75 was neutral (E040), but the cyclic form lowers momentum where the steps are largest. Keep if dev gains >=0.1 pp and official >=0.7535. A |delta| <0.1 pp closes the Muon-momentum axis.
description: Explore a time-free Muon schedule knob (D004 C0029/C0030, cyclical momentum). On the E059 tip, turn the Muon momentum from a graph constant into a per-step GPU schedule tensor that runs opposite to the LR triangle: 0.72 at step 0, falling linearly to 0.60 at peak LR, then rising linearly back to 0.72 at the end (mean ≈ the current 0.655). The Nesterov form, lr, SGD groups, Lookahead, resolutions and everything else stay fixed. Recapture all graphs in build. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, about 5.24 s). Dev mean moves -0.25 to +0.25 pp from 0.7586, with a weak prior of +0.0 to +0.15 pp: each earlier halving gave +0.27-0.29 pp, but the response must flatten near the references' ratio. Keep if the dev gain is at least 0.1 pp and official is at least 0.7535. The added margin would be spent on the group-2 width cut or the 24 px epoch drop.
description: Exploit: the pre-registered BN-bias follow-up, which adds margin at no time cost. On the E061 tip (2/2/3 net, 2x20+3x24+3x28+2.5x32 px, head scale 2x, ls 0.4, BN-bias lr multiplier 16x; official 0.7560, dev 0.7586 @ 5.24 s), halve the BN-bias lr multiplier from 16x to 8x. Change nothing else: Muon lr and momentum, head lr, SGD-group wd and momentum, schedule, Lookahead, resolutions, freezing and the whitening-bias window all stay fixed. If the multiplier lives in the GPU schedule tensor, no recapture is needed; otherwise recapture all graphs in build. Log the absolute BN-bias:head lr ratio before and after (the references sit at about 1:10-1:13). Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12 and compare against E061's dev mean of 0.7586. Contingency: if dev rises by 0.15 pp or more, try 4x next. If dev falls by 0.15 pp or more, 16x brackets the optimum and the BN-bias axis is closed.

expected: Time falls 6-11% (about 4.65-4.95 s). The 16x16→8x8 group-2 convs and the 320→576 entry lose about 17-31% of their MACs, plus smaller NS Grams. Dev mean falls 0.1-0.4 pp, centred near -0.25 pp, i.e. at or better than 0.67 pp/s (the 32 px tail rate). Keep if dev is at least 0.7558 and official at least 0.753. If dev lands in 0.754-0.7558, bank the cut to stack with the next margin source, such as BN-bias 8x. This is removed work, so it should carry over to the PCIe judge.
description: Exploit: width-based work removal in group 2, the cheapest remaining structural lever now that the depth floors are reached. First microbenchmark ms/step per phase on the E061 recipe (graphed, Muon included) for group 2 at width 384 vs 320, in both of its convs. Widening to 448 cost +13.6% per trial, so a large saving is expected. If 320 saves at least 4% per trial, narrow group 2 from 384 to 320 on the E061 tip: adjust the group-3 entry conv (320→576), the group-2 BN params and the Muon batched-NS shape groups. Hold epochs, resolutions, schedule, ls, head scale, BN-bias multiplier, freezing and the bias window fixed. Recapture all graphs in build. Check that eval returns finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If the microbenchmark saves under 3%, log it and do not run.

expected: Time falls 0.3-0.42 s (-6 to -8%, to about 4.85 s). On the 2/2/3 net, a 20 px epoch measured +0.34 s in E063, and a 24 px epoch costs somewhat more. Dev mean changes by -0.25 to +0.05 pp, centred near -0.1 pp. Keep if dev is at least 0.7558 and official at least 0.753. A dev loss under 0.1 pp supports H1.11, makes the 2x20+2x24 ladder the new base, and makes H1.11.2 (spend the saving on +0.5 epoch at 32 px) the follow-up. A loss of 0.3 pp or more means the 24 px rung does feature learning that the 28 px phase cannot absorb.
description: Exploit: remove an early low-res epoch, since E036 and E063 show the early phase is saturated. On the E061 tip, drop one 24 px epoch, giving 2x20+2x24+3x28+2.5x32 (32 fewer steps). Fix the LR warmup length and the Lookahead alpha ramp in absolute steps at their E061 values, so the decay portion absorbs the shortfall; this reuses the anchoring code path from E063. The whitening-bias window (20 px phase only) and the conv1 freeze at 32 px are unchanged. Same 4 graphs, nothing new to capture. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12 and compare against E061's dev mean of 0.7586.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Dev mean moves -0.25 to +0.25 pp, with no strong prior on sign (weak lean +0.05 pp, since the BN-bias halvings also gained). Keep if the dev gain is at least 0.1 pp and official is at least 0.7535.
description: Exploit, separating the two knobs that E053 confounded. On the E061 tip, keep the head output scale at 2x and halve the head-weight lr (in the SGD head group), changing nothing else. Under Agarwala et al., the effective head lr scales as lr·β², so the 2x scale also quadrupled the effective head step. Halving the lr tests whether part of E053's +0.44 pp came from temperature and part was a too-large head step. The lr is a per-group value in the schedule tensor, so recapture only if it is a graph constant. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. Contingency: if dev falls by 0.15 pp or more, run 2x head lr next. If |Δ| < 0.1 pp, the head lr is not a live knob at this scale; close H1.10.2.

expected: Metrics unchanged (5.24 s). Held-out mean 0.7566-0.7581, i.e. 0.05-0.2 pp below the dev mean of 0.7586, with per-seed std 0.2-0.3 pp rather than E061's 0.13. Decision rule: if the held-out mean is below 0.7558, raise the dev keep bar for time cuts by the measured bias and prioritize margin sources (BN-bias 8x, head lr) before the group-2 width or 24 px cuts. If it is at least 0.7575, dev is unbiased and the current keep bar stands.
description: Calibration against the winner's curse, with no recipe change and nothing kept. Run the E061 tip code unchanged on fresh held-out seeds 13-22 (10 trials) outside the official command, using the existing trial-seed plumbing. Log per-seed accuracy and time. Seeds 13-22 then stay out of all selection, and are used only for the final pre-submission check of whichever tip exists at the end. Dev seeds 3-12 have now driven about 6 keep decisions (E053, E054, E055, E056, E058, E061), so the dev mean of the current tip is likely biased upward.

expected: Time rises by about 0.08-0.15 s (+1.5-3%), from one more batched NS step over about 330 steps on the 2/2/3 matrices. Dev mean rises 0.0 to +0.25 pp, centred near +0.1 pp. To beat the 32 px tail exchange rate (0.67 pp/s), it needs at least about 0.1 pp per +0.15 s; if so, it becomes a margin source to pay for the group-2 width cut. A gain under 0.1 pp means AOL + 2 already saturates quality, and H1.12 is closed.
description: Explore whether orthogonalization quality is still below saturation, a margin source the tree has not tested since E035 and E052 showed steep losses below the current budget. On the E061 tip, add a third fixed-coefficient quintic Newton-Schulz step after AOL preconditioning (AOL + 3), keeping lr 0.205, momentum 0.655 and the per-step renorm. Change nothing else. Recapture all graphs in build. Log Muon ms/step per phase. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12.

expected: Time +0.3-1% (one masked fill per epoch on GPU). Dev mean moves -0.3 to +0.25 pp, with no strong prior: the gap argues for a gain, while airbench Appendix B finds Cutout hurts at 10 epochs or fewer. Keep if the dev gain is at least 0.15 pp and official is at least 0.7535. If |Δ| < 0.1 pp, input regularization is not the binding axis, and H1.3.2 and H1.3.5 should be deprioritized.
description: Explore input regularization, given E060's 21 pp train-test gap (variance-limited, not under-fit). On the E061 tip, add GPU-side Cutout with an 8 px square (at 32 px coordinates, applied before downscaling) to training images only during the 24 px and 28 px phases. The 20 px phase and the 2.5-epoch 32 px tail stay clean, so the final fit matches the test distribution. Draw the masks per epoch with the trial-seeded generator inside the existing un-graphed per-epoch augmentation, so no graph changes. Change nothing else. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12.

expected: Time falls 0.3-1% (about -0.02 to -0.05 s): no BN-weight gradient reductions and one less foreach update. Dev mean within ±0.1 pp of 0.7586, or slightly up, since both Muon references drop the BN scale under per-step weight renorm. Keep if time is at least 0.3% lower, dev is at least 0.7558 and official at least 0.753. A dev loss of 0.15 pp or more means the BN scale carries useful per-channel gain here.
description: Exploit with a small work-removal cut, gated on a code check. First inspect the E061 BN modules. If BN weights are trainable or eps differs from the references, freeze BN weight at 1 (requires_grad False, removed from the SGD group) with eps 1e-12, matching airbench94_muon and Hiverge, in every block. Change nothing else. Recapture all graphs in build. If the port already matches, close H1.7.13 without a run. Otherwise run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12.
note: Code check: the port already matches — BatchNorm has eps=1e-12 and weight.requires_grad=False (frozen at 1) in every block since E001; nothing to change.

expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, about 4.85 s). Dev mean moves -0.3 to +0.3 pp from 0.7573, leaning +0.05 to +0.2 pp: the halving lost 0.35 pp, so the head step may still be below its optimum. Keep if the dev gain is at least 0.1 pp and official is at least 0.753. Any gain of 0.2 pp or more is the margin that licenses stacking the banked group-2 width cut (320).
description: Exploit: the pre-registered contingency from E068. Halving the head lr cost 0.35 pp on dev, so test the opposite direction. On the current tip (E067 code as committed: 2/2/3 net, 2x20+2x24+3x28+2.5x32 px with warmup and Lookahead anchored in absolute steps, head output scale 2x, ls 0.4, BN-bias multiplier as in E067; official 0.7544, dev 0.7573, held-out 0.7562 @ 4.85 s), double the head-weight lr in the SGD head group, keep the head scale at 2x and change nothing else. If the lr is a value in the GPU schedule tensor, nothing needs recapturing; otherwise recapture all graphs in build. Log the absolute head:BN-bias lr ratio. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12; do not touch held-out seeds 13-22. Contingency: if dev rises by 0.15 pp or more, try 3x the head lr next. If dev falls by 0.15 pp or more, the head lr is bracketed at 1x and H1.10.2 closes.

expected: Time falls about 0.25-0.3 s (-5 to -6%, to about 4.55-4.6 s on E067's ladder; E066 measured -0.28 s). Dev mean falls 0.2-0.4 pp, centred near -0.3 pp, which is E066's rate of about 1.1 pp/s. Keep if dev is at least 0.7558 and official at least 0.753. This is removed work, so it should carry over to the PCIe judge.
description: Exploit, stacking a banked cut once margin exists. Run this only after the head-lr idea (and/or AOL+3, Cutout or SGD momentum) has produced a kept tip whose dev mean is at least 0.7590, i.e. about +0.2 pp over E067's 0.7573. On that tip, narrow group 2 from 384 to 320 channels in both of its convs, exactly as in E066. Adjust the group-3 entry conv (320→576), the group-2 BN params and the Muon batched-NS shape groups. Hold everything else fixed and recapture all graphs in build. Check that eval returns finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If no margin source has passed, leave this queued; do not run it on E067, whose held-out expectation (0.7562) minus E066's measured -0.32 pp would land on the bar.
note: Its precondition is not met: it should run only on a kept tip with dev mean >= 0.7590; the tip E067 has dev 0.7573 and the margin ideas since (head lr x0.5/x2, AOL+3) did not raise it. Re-add when such a tip exists.

expected: Time falls 1-3% (about -0.05 to -0.15 s, to about 4.7-4.8 s). Accuracy should be bit-identical per seed. If there is any difference, it must come from fp rounding and stay within ±0.05 pp on dev. Keep if time is at least 0.7% lower and official is at least 0.753. The probable target is the un-graphed per-epoch augmentation, which grows in share as epochs get cheaper (about 9.5 epochs in 4.85 s).
description: Exploit, a numerically identical overhead cut found by profiling first. On the E067 tip, capture one trial with torch.profiler in a dev-only run outside the official command. Record per phase the top-20 GPU kernels by self time, plus the CPU-side and un-graphed work between graph replays: per-epoch crop/flip/interpolate/normalize, index generation, Lookahead copies and per-phase switching. Log what share of train time is outside graph replay. If any single item is at least 1% of train time, remove the largest one while keeping RNG draws and outputs bit-identical. For example, fuse the per-epoch crop+flip+downscale into one compiled function warmed up in build at every phase resolution, or fold the Lookahead copy into the graphed step. Change nothing else. Run the official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If nothing reaches 1%, log the breakdown, close H2.6.3 and make no run. Also record the per-layer conv share, which feeds H2.7.1.

expected: If the offline check passes, Muon GPU time falls 25-40%, so total time falls about 0.1-0.17 s (-2 to -3.5%). Dev mean stays within ±0.1 pp of 0.7573. Keep if time is at least 1.5% lower, dev is at least 0.7558 and official is at least 0.753. This is removed matmul work, so it should carry over to the judge. There is a substantial (~40%) prior that the fp16 check fails, which would close the branch cheaply without an official run.
description: Explore, cutting Muon cost, which is now about 1.5 ms/step × ~330 steps ≈ 0.45 s, roughly 9% of a 4.85 s trial. First run an offline check on 3 sets of real momentum-gradient matrices captured from dev training steps (early, mid and late, at each conv shape), not Gaussian ones (the E035 lesson). Compare 2-iteration Gram Newton-Schulz against the current AOL+2 quintic steps. Gram NS iterates the polynomial on the n×n Gram (small side) and applies it to X once, in fp16 with a 1.05 safety factor, starting from the AOL-scaled Gram that already exists.
